evidence: PR #1273 merged the deterministic read-only experiment simplification helper and focused fixtures at 161aa4bd2a5b7581fb2c61747ec2e4ef4d168cdb after Experiment Lifecycle, Data Architecture, Storage Health and Automation Production Health gates passed.

Follow-up PR #1277 merged the current-registry non-mutation regression at 10ffabb6e8ad77fdc7cf1bb27a8c1c7a403b9746; Experiment Lifecycle Gate run 35930222499 passed against the live registry/candidate corpus.

The live-registry regression runs the review twice, requires deterministic identical output, hashes every candidate JSON before and after and requires byte-for-byte equality, and reasserts zero automatic merge, retirement, promotion, model-weight, market-gate or portfolio authority.

Current registry readback exposed 387 registry rows, 379 unique candidate IDs and 8 duplicate-ID legacy families; the implementation preserves these as explicit read-only registry-duplication diagnostics rather than silently deleting, merging or treating them as hypothesis diversity.
Exact semantic alias clustering uses existing canonical metric normalization and full semantic identity; same target path alone remains explicitly insufficient merge authority.

requirements.text: Implement the smallest deterministic read-only simplification review over the existing Experiment Lifecycle registry that flags semantic/path alias families, high-observation zero-outcome incubation and repeated matured-inconclusive families for governance review without automatically merging, retiring, promoting or changing weights.
Equivalent known path-alias candidates with the same kind/direction/horizon are grouped with every original candidate ID preserved.
The report separately flags high-observation zero-outcome incubation and repeated matured-inconclusive families.
Distinct hypotheses are not collapsed solely because they share a metric path.
No candidate is deleted, rewritten, auto-retired, auto-merged, promoted or assigned a model weight by the review.
